405
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# cargo-vet ratchet baseline: the number of unvetted dependencies.
# The FIRST bare-number line of this file is the baseline.
#
# 437 was the first real measurement in which cargo-vet actually RAN in this
# repository (2026-07-26). Before that supply-chain/config.toml contained
# invented keys so the tool fell over with a parse error; the file's existence
# gave the impression of auditing, but not a single dependency had been audited.
# The count fell to 434 on 2026-09-04 and to 433 on 2026-09-06 after the
# libp2p-connection-limits audit. With libp2p 0.57.1 from crates.io and the
# obsolete git-fork policies removed, cargo-vet 0.10.2 measured 409 on
# 2026-11-13 (Linux x86_64, Rust 1.97.1). This lowers the ratchet by 24.
# The history below keeps the earlier 437 measurement as evidence.
#
# Rule: this number MUST NOT RISE. Lowering it is free and encouraged - when it
# drops, this file is lowered in a deliberate PR (the ratchet tightens). Raising
# the number counts as CI softening.
#
# Import coverage was measured (2026-07-26): `cargo vet regenerate imports`
# pulled 268 audit records for 158 crates from six trusted sources (Mozilla,
# Google, Bytecode Alliance, ISRG, Embark, Zcash) - imports.lock is 74 KB. Even
# so the number stayed at 437 then: the measurement gave an identical result
# with imports.lock full and completely empty (437 = 437, zero crates closed).
# The reason is that cargo-vet requires an exact version/delta match; the
# fetched audits do not cover our locked versions. So the baseline is NOT
# inflated by "imports not fetched yet", it shows the real audit debt.
#
# Debt paydown priority (the crypto/FFI surface first):
#   ring, pqcrypto-dilithium, cryptoki, bls12_381, aes-gcm, chacha20
#
# 2026-11-19: 409 -> 405. Dropping the unused default feature of a
# serialization dependency removed a fixed-capacity collection crate and its
# three transitive crates from all three lockfiles, so four entries left the
# unvetted set. The gate printed the improvement line itself, so the ratchet is
# tightened in the same breath: `cargo-vet 0.10.3` on the pinned toolchain now
# reports `unvetted dependencies: 405 | baseline: 405` with no slack. Tightened
# on this branch and on the one it merges into together, so no branch carries a
# ratchet sitting above the debt it measures.
